blocks.source: # CHAPTER 12  INVERSE FUNCTIONS
blocks.translation: # 第 12 章　反函数

blocks.source: We now have at our disposal quite powerful methods for investigating functions; what we lack is an adequate supply of functions to which these methods may be applied. We have studied various ways of forming new functions from old—addition, multiplication, division, and composition—but using these alone, we can produce only the rational functions (even the sine function, although frequently used for examples, has never been defined). In the next few chapters we will begin to construct new functions in quite sophisticated ways, but there is one important method which will practically double the usefulness of any other method we discover.
blocks.translation: 现在，我们已经掌握了研究函数的相当有力的方法；所缺少的是足够多的函数，好让这些方法有用武之地。我们研究过从旧函数构造新函数的各种方法——加、乘、除以及复合——但单靠这些方法，我们只能得到有理函数（连经常被用作例子的正弦函数，也从未得到定义）。接下来的几章中，我们将开始用相当精巧的方法构造新函数，不过有一种重要的方法，几乎能让我们发现的其他任何方法的用途翻一番。

blocks.translation: 回想函数是一族数对，我们也许会想到一个妙主意：只要把所有数对的次序颠倒过来就行了。于是，从函数

blocks.source: we obtain
blocks.translation: 我们得到

blocks.source: While $f(1)=2$ and $f(3)=4$, we have $g(2)=1$ and $g(4)=3$.
Unfortunately, this bright idea does not always work. If
blocks.translation: 可惜，这个妙主意并不总是奏效。如果

blocks.source: then the collection
blocks.translation: 那么，数对的集合

blocks.source: is not a function at all, since it contains both $(4,3)$ and $(4,13)$. It is clear where the trouble lies: $f(3)=f(13)$, even though $3\ne13$. This is the only sort of thing that can go wrong, and it is worthwhile giving a name to the functions for which this does not happen.
blocks.translation: 根本不是函数，因为它同时包含 $(4,3)$ 和 $(4,13)$。问题显然出在这里：尽管 $3\ne13$，却有 $f(3)=f(13)$。可能出的问题只有这一种，值得给不会发生这种情况的函数起个名字。

blocks.source: **DEFINITION**
A function $f$ is **one-one** (read “one-to-one”) if $f(a)\ne f(b)$ whenever $a\ne b$.
blocks.translation: 如果每当 $a\ne b$ 时都有 $f(a)\ne f(b)$，就称函数 $f$ 是**一一的**（读作“一对一”）。

blocks.source: The identity function $I$ is obviously one-one, and so is the following modification:
blocks.translation: 恒等函数 $I$ 显然是一一的，下面这个改造后的函数也是：

blocks.source: $$g(x)=\begin{cases}x,&x\ne3,5\\3,&x=5\\5,&x=3.\end{cases}$$
The function $f(x)=x^2$ is not one-one, since $f(-1)=f(1)$, but if we define
blocks.translation: 函数 $f(x)=x^2$ 不是一一的，因为 $f(-1)=f(1)$；但如果定义

blocks.source: $$g(x)=x^2,\qquad x\ge0$$
(and leave $g$ undefined for $x<0$), then $g$ is one-one, because $g$ is increasing (since $g'(x)=2x>0$, for $x>0$). This observation is easily generalized: If $n$ is a natural number and
blocks.translation: （并且让 $g$ 在 $x<0$ 时无定义），那么 $g$ 就是一一的，因为 $g$ 是递增的（这是因为，在 $x>0$ 时，$g'(x)=2x>0$）。这一观察很容易推广：如果 $n$ 是自然数，并且

blocks.source: $$f(x)=x^n,\qquad x\ge0,$$
then $f$ is one-one. If $n$ is odd, one can do better: the function
blocks.translation: 那么 $f$ 就是一一的。如果 $n$ 是奇数，还可以做得更好：函数

blocks.source: $$f(x)=x^n\quad\text{for all }x$$
is one-one (since $f'(x)=nx^{n-1}>0$, for all $x\ne0$).
blocks.translation: 是一一的（因为对所有 $x\ne0$ 都有 $f'(x)=nx^{n-1}>0$）。

blocks.source: It is particularly easy to decide from the graph of $f$ whether $f$ is one-one: the condition $f(a)\ne f(b)$ for $a\ne b$ means that no *horizontal* line intersects the graph of $f$ twice (Figure 1).
blocks.translation: 从 $f$ 的图像判断 $f$ 是否一一，格外容易：在 $a\ne b$ 时有 $f(a)\ne f(b)$ 这一条件，意味着没有任何一条*水平*直线与 $f$ 的图像相交两次（图 1）。

blocks.source: If we reverse all the pairs in (a not necessarily one-one function) $f$ we obtain, in any case, some collection of pairs. It is popular to abstain from this procedure unless $f$ is one-one, but there is no particular reason to do so—instead of a definition with restrictive conditions we obtain a definition and a theorem.
blocks.translation: 如果把（不一定一一的函数）$f$ 中所有数对的次序都颠倒过来，无论如何都会得到某个数对集合。通常的做法是，除非 $f$ 是一一的，否则不这样做；但并没有什么特别的理由一定要如此——我们可以得到一个定义和一个定理，而不是一个附有限制条件的定义。

blocks.source: **DEFINITION**
For any function $f$, the **inverse** of $f$, denoted by $f^{-1}$, is the set of all pairs $(a,b)$ for which the pair $(b,a)$ is in $f$.
blocks.translation: 对于任意函数 $f$，$f$ 的**逆**记作 $f^{-1}$，它是由所有这样的数对 $(a,b)$ 组成的集合：数对 $(b,a)$ 属于 $f$。

blocks.source: **THEOREM 1**
$f^{-1}$ is a function if and only if $f$ is one-one.
blocks.translation: $f^{-1}$ 是函数，当且仅当 $f$ 是一一的。

blocks.source: **PROOF** Suppose first that $f$ is one-one. Let $(a,b)$ and $(a,c)$ be two pairs in $f^{-1}$. Then $(b,a)$ and $(c,a)$ are in $f$, so $a=f(b)$ and $a=f(c)$; since $f$ is one-one this implies that $b=c$. Thus $f^{-1}$ is a function.
blocks.translation: **证明** 首先假设 $f$ 是一一的。设 $(a,b)$ 和 $(a,c)$ 是 $f^{-1}$ 中的两个数对。那么 $(b,a)$ 和 $(c,a)$ 属于 $f$，所以 $a=f(b)$ 且 $a=f(c)$；由于 $f$ 是一一的，这就意味着 $b=c$。因此 $f^{-1}$ 是函数。

blocks.source: Conversely, suppose that $f^{-1}$ is a function. If $f(b)=f(c)$, then $f$ contains the pairs $(b,f(b))$ and $(c,f(c))=(c,f(b))$, so $(f(b),b)$ and $(f(b),c)$ are in $f^{-1}$. Since $f^{-1}$ is a function this implies that $b=c$. Thus $f$ is one-one. $\blacksquare$
blocks.translation: 反过来，假设 $f^{-1}$ 是函数。如果 $f(b)=f(c)$，那么 $f$ 包含数对 $(b,f(b))$ 和 $(c,f(c))=(c,f(b))$，所以 $(f(b),b)$ 和 $(f(b),c)$ 都属于 $f^{-1}$。由于 $f^{-1}$ 是函数，这就意味着 $b=c$。因此 $f$ 是一一的。$\blacksquare$

blocks.source: The graphs of $f$ and $f^{-1}$ are so closely related that it is possible to use the graph of $f$ to visualize the graph of $f^{-1}$. Since the graph of $f^{-1}$ consists of all pairs $(a,b)$ with $(b,a)$ in the graph of $f$, one obtains the graph of $f^{-1}$ from the graph of $f$ by interchanging the horizontal and vertical axes. If $f$ has the graph shown in Figure 2(a),
blocks.translation: $f$ 与 $f^{-1}$ 的图像关系十分密切，因此可以借助 $f$ 的图像来想象 $f^{-1}$ 的图像。由于 $f^{-1}$ 的图像由所有这样的数对 $(a,b)$ 组成：$(b,a)$ 在 $f$ 的图像上，因此只需交换横轴和纵轴，就能由 $f$ 的图像得到 $f^{-1}$ 的图像。如果 $f$ 的图像如图 2(a) 所示，

blocks.source: and you rotate this page counter clockwise through a right angle, then the graph of $f^{-1}$ appears on your left (Figure 2(b)). The only trouble is that the numbering on the horizontal axis goes in the wrong direction, so you must flip this picture over, to get the usual picture of $f^{-1}$, which appears on your right (Figure 3).
blocks.translation: 而你把本页逆时针旋转一个直角，那么 $f^{-1}$ 的图像就出现在你的左边（图 2(b)）。唯一的问题是，横轴上数字的排列方向反了，因此还必须把这幅图翻过来，才能得到通常的 $f^{-1}$ 图像，它会出现在你的右边（图 3）。

blocks.source: This procedure is awkward with books and impossible with blackboards, so it is fortunate that there is another way of constructing the graph of $f^{-1}$. The points
blocks.translation: 对书本来说，这种操作很不方便；对黑板来说，根本不可能。幸好，还有另一种构造 $f^{-1}$ 图像的方法。点

blocks.source: $(a,b)$ and $(b,a)$ are reflections of each other through the graph of $I(x)=x$, which is called the **diagonal** (Figure 4). To obtain the graph of $f^{-1}$ we merely reflect the graph of $f$ through this line (Figure 5).
blocks.translation: $(a,b)$ 和 $(b,a)$ 关于 $I(x)=x$ 的图像互相对称，这条直线称为**对角线**（图 4）。只需将 $f$ 的图像关于这条直线作反射，就能得到 $f^{-1}$ 的图像（图 5）。

blocks.source: Reflecting through the diagonal twice will clearly leave us right back where we started; this means that $(f^{-1})^{-1}=f$, which is also clear from the definition. In conjunction with Theorem 1, this equation has a significant consequence: if $f$ is a one-one function, then the function $f^{-1}$ is also one-one (since $(f^{-1})^{-1}$ is a function).
blocks.translation: 关于对角线连续反射两次，显然会回到原来的位置；这意味着 $(f^{-1})^{-1}=f$，而从定义也能看出这一点。结合定理 1，这个等式有一个重要推论：如果 $f$ 是一一函数，那么函数 $f^{-1}$ 也是一一的（因为 $(f^{-1})^{-1}$ 是函数）。

blocks.source: There are a few other simple manipulations with inverse functions of which you should be aware. Since $(a,b)$ is in $f$ precisely when $(b,a)$ is in $f^{-1}$, it follows that
blocks.translation: 还有几种有关反函数的简单运算，你应当熟悉。由于 $(a,b)$ 属于 $f$ 当且仅当 $(b,a)$ 属于 $f^{-1}$，因此

blocks.source: $$b=f(a)\quad\text{means the same as}\quad a=f^{-1}(b).$$

Thus $f^{-1}(b)$ is the (unique) number $a$ such that $f(a)=b$; for example, if $f(x)=x^3$, then $f^{-1}(b)$ is the unique number $a$ such that $a^3=b$, and this number is, by definition, $\sqrt[3]{b}$.
blocks.translation: 所以，$f^{-1}(b)$ 就是使得 $f(a)=b$ 的那个（唯一的）数 $a$；例如，若 $f(x)=x^3$，则 $f^{-1}(b)$ 是使得 $a^3=b$ 的唯一的数 $a$，而这个数按定义就是 $\sqrt[3]{b}$。

blocks.source: The fact that $f^{-1}(x)$ is the number $y$ such that $f(y)=x$ can be restated in a much more compact form:
blocks.translation: $f^{-1}(x)$ 是满足 $f(y)=x$ 的数 $y$ 这一事实，可以用简洁得多的形式重述：

blocks.source: $$f(f^{-1}(x))=x,\quad\text{for all }x\text{ in the domain of }f^{-1}.$$
Moreover,
blocks.translation: 此外，

blocks.source: $$f^{-1}(f(x))=x,\quad\text{for all }x\text{ in the domain of }f;$$
this follows from the previous equation upon replacing $f$ by $f^{-1}$. These two important equations can be written
blocks.translation: 在前一个等式中把 $f$ 换成 $f^{-1}$，就能得到这个式子。这两个重要等式可以写成

blocks.source: $$\begin{aligned}f\circ f^{-1}&=I,\\f^{-1}\circ f&=I\end{aligned}$$
(except that the right side will have a bigger domain if the domain of $f$ or $f^{-1}$ is not all of $\mathbf R$).
blocks.translation: （不过，如果 $f$ 或 $f^{-1}$ 的定义域不是整个 $\mathbf R$，那么右边的定义域会更大）。

blocks.source: Since many standard functions will be defined as the inverses of other functions, it is quite important that we be able to tell which functions are one-one. We have already hinted which class of functions are most easily dealt with—increasing and decreasing functions are obviously one-one. Moreover, if $f$ is increasing, then $f^{-1}$ is also increasing, and if $f$ is decreasing, then $f^{-1}$ is decreasing (the proof is left to you). In addition, $f$ is increasing if and only if $-f$ is decreasing, a very useful fact to remember.
blocks.translation: 许多常见函数都将被定义为其他函数的反函数，因此，能够判断哪些函数是一一的十分重要。我们已经暗示过，哪一类函数最容易处理——递增函数和递减函数显然都是一一的。此外，若 $f$ 递增，$f^{-1}$ 也递增；若 $f$ 递减，$f^{-1}$ 也递减（证明留给你）。另外，$f$ 递增当且仅当 $-f$ 递减，这是一个很值得记住的事实。

blocks.source: It is certainly not true that every one-one function is either increasing or decreasing. One example has already been mentioned, and is now graphed in Figure 6:
blocks.translation: 并非每个一一函数都非增即减。我们已经提到过一个例子，现在将它画在图 6 中：

blocks.source: $$g(x)=\begin{cases}x,&x\ne3,5\\3,&x=5\\5,&x=3.\end{cases}$$

Figure 7 shows that there are even continuous one-one functions which are neither increasing nor decreasing. But if you try drawing a few pictures you will soon suspect that every one-one continuous function defined on an interval is either increasing or decreasing.
blocks.translation: 图 7 表明，甚至存在既不递增也不递减的连续一一函数。不过，只要试着画几幅图，你很快就会猜想：定义在一个区间上的每个连续一一函数，不是递增的，就是递减的。

blocks.source: **THEOREM 2**
If $f$ is continuous and one-one on an interval, then $f$ is either increasing or decreasing on that interval.
blocks.translation: 如果 $f$ 在一个区间上连续且一一，那么 $f$ 在该区间上不是递增的，就是递减的。

blocks.source: **PROOF** The proof proceeds in three easy steps:
blocks.translation: **证明** 证明分为三个简单步骤：

blocks.source: (1) If $a<b<c$ are three points in the interval, then
blocks.translation: (1) 如果 $a<b<c$ 是区间中的三个点，那么

blocks.source: $$\begin{array}{rll}\text{either}&\text{(i)}&f(a)<f(b)<f(c)\\\text{or}&\text{(ii)}&f(a)>f(b)>f(c).\end{array}$$
Suppose, for example, that $f(a)<f(c)$. If we had $f(b)<f(a)$ (Figure 8), then the Intermediate Value Theorem applied to the interval $[b,c]$ would give an $x$ with
blocks.translation: 例如，假设 $f(a)<f(c)$。如果 $f(b)<f(a)$（图 8），那么在区间 $[b,c]$ 上应用介值定理，就会得到某个 $x$，使得

blocks.source: $b<x<c$ and $f(x)=f(a)$, contradicting the fact that $f$ is one-one on $[a,c]$. Similarly, $f(b)>f(c)$ would lead to a contradiction, so $f(a)<f(b)<f(c)$.
blocks.translation: $b<x<c$ 且 $f(x)=f(a)$，这与 $f$ 在 $[a,c]$ 上一一相矛盾。同样，$f(b)>f(c)$ 也会导致矛盾，所以 $f(a)<f(b)<f(c)$。

blocks.source: Naturally, the same sort of argument works for the case $f(a)>f(c)$.
blocks.translation: 当然，对于 $f(a)>f(c)$ 的情形，同样的论证仍然适用。

blocks.source: (2) If $a<b<c<d$ are four points in the interval, then
blocks.translation: (2) 如果 $a<b<c<d$ 是区间中的四个点，那么

blocks.source: $$\begin{array}{rll}\text{either}&\text{(i)}&f(a)<f(b)<f(c)<f(d)\\\text{or}&\text{(ii)}&f(a)>f(b)>f(c)>f(d).\end{array}$$
For we can apply (1) to $a<b<c$ and then to $b<c<d$.
blocks.translation: 因为我们可以先对 $a<b<c$ 应用 (1)，再对 $b<c<d$ 应用 (1)。

blocks.source: (3) Take any $a<b$ in the interval, and suppose that $f(a)<f(b)$. Then $f$ is increasing: For if $c$ and $d$ are any two points, we can apply (2) to the collection $\{a,b,c,d\}$ (after arranging them in increasing order). $\blacksquare$
blocks.translation: (3) 在区间内任取 $a<b$，并假设 $f(a)<f(b)$。那么 $f$ 就是递增的：因为，对于任意两个点 $c$ 和 $d$，我们都可以对集合 $\{a,b,c,d\}$ 应用 (2)（先将它们按从小到大的次序排列）。$\blacksquare$

blocks.source: Henceforth we shall be concerned almost exclusively with continuous increasing or decreasing functions which are defined on an interval. If $f$ is such a function, it is possible to say quite precisely what the domain of $f^{-1}$ will be like.
blocks.translation: 从现在起，我们所关心的几乎都是定义在一个区间上的连续递增函数或连续递减函数。若 $f$ 是这样的函数，就可以相当精确地说明 $f^{-1}$ 的定义域是什么样子。

blocks.source: Suppose first that $f$ is a continuous increasing function on the closed interval $[a,b]$. Then, by the Intermediate Value Theorem, $f$ takes on every value between $f(a)$ and $f(b)$. Therefore, the domain of $f^{-1}$ is the closed interval $[f(a),f(b)]$. Similarly, if $f$ is continuous and decreasing on $[a,b]$, then the domain of $f^{-1}$ is $[f(b),f(a)]$.
blocks.translation: 先假设 $f$ 是闭区间 $[a,b]$ 上的连续递增函数。那么由介值定理，$f$ 取遍 $f(a)$ 与 $f(b)$ 之间的所有值。因此，$f^{-1}$ 的定义域就是闭区间 $[f(a),f(b)]$。同样，若 $f$ 在 $[a,b]$ 上连续且递减，则 $f^{-1}$ 的定义域是 $[f(b),f(a)]$。

blocks.source: If $f$ is a continuous increasing function on an *open* interval $(a,b)$ the analysis becomes a bit more difficult. To begin with, let us choose some point $c$ in $(a,b)$. We will first decide which values $>f(c)$ are taken on by $f$. One possibility is that $f$ takes on arbitrarily large values (Figure 9). In this case $f$ takes on all values $>f(c)$, by the Intermediate Value Theorem. If, on the other hand, $f$ does not take on arbitrarily large values, then $A=\{f(x):c\le x<b\}$ is bounded above, so $A$ has a least upper bound $\alpha$ (Figure 10). Now suppose $y$ is any number with $f(c)<y<\alpha$. Then $f$ takes on some value $f(x)>y$ (because $\alpha$ is the least upper bound of $A$). By the Intermediate Value Theorem, $f$ actually takes on the value $y$. Notice that $f$ cannot take on the value $\alpha$ itself; for if $\alpha=f(x)$ for $a<x<b$ and we choose $t$ with $x<t<b$, then $f(t)>\alpha$, which is impossible.
blocks.translation: 如果 $f$ 是*开*区间 $(a,b)$ 上的连续递增函数，分析就稍微困难一些。首先，在 $(a,b)$ 中选取一点 $c$。我们先来判断，$f$ 会取到哪些 $>f(c)$ 的值。一种可能是，$f$ 取到任意大的值（图 9）。这时由介值定理，$f$ 取遍所有 $>f(c)$ 的值。另一方面，如果 $f$ 不取到任意大的值，那么 $A=\{f(x):c\le x<b\}$ 有上界，所以 $A$ 有最小上界 $\alpha$（图 10）。现在设 $y$ 是满足 $f(c)<y<\alpha$ 的任意一个数。那么 $f$ 会取到某个值 $f(x)>y$（因为 $\alpha$ 是 $A$ 的最小上界）。由介值定理，$f$ 实际上会取到值 $y$。注意，$f$ 不可能取到 $\alpha$ 本身；因为，若对某个 $a<x<b$ 有 $\alpha=f(x)$，再选取满足 $x<t<b$ 的 $t$，便会有 $f(t)>\alpha$，这是不可能的。

blocks.source: Precisely the same arguments work for values less than $f(c)$; either $f$ takes on all values less than $f(c)$ or there is a number $\beta<f(c)$ such that $f$ takes on all values between $\beta$ and $f(c)$, but not $\beta$ itself.
blocks.translation: 对小于 $f(c)$ 的值，完全相同的论证也适用：或者 $f$ 取遍所有小于 $f(c)$ 的值，或者存在一个数 $\beta<f(c)$，使得 $f$ 取遍 $\beta$ 和 $f(c)$ 之间的所有值，却不取到 $\beta$ 本身。

blocks.source: This entire argument can be repeated if $f$ is decreasing, and if the domain of $f$ is $\mathbf R$ or $(a,\infty)$ or $(-\infty,a)$. Summarizing: if $f$ is a continuous increasing, or decreasing, function whose domain is an interval having one of the forms $(a,b)$, $(-\infty,b)$, $(a,\infty)$, or $\mathbf R$, then the domain of $f^{-1}$ is also an interval which has one of these four forms, and we can easily fit the remaining types of intervals, $(a,b]$, $[a,b]$, $(-\infty,b]$, and $[a,\infty)$, into this discussion also.
blocks.translation: 如果 $f$ 递减，或者 $f$ 的定义域是 $\mathbf R$、$(a,\infty)$ 或 $(-\infty,a)$，整个论证都可以重复。概括起来：如果 $f$ 是连续递增函数或连续递减函数，其定义域是形如 $(a,b)$、$(-\infty,b)$、$(a,\infty)$ 或 $\mathbf R$ 的区间，那么 $f^{-1}$ 的定义域也具有这四种形式之一；其余类型的区间 $(a,b]$、$[a,b]$、$(-\infty,b]$ 和 $[a,\infty)$，也很容易纳入这一讨论。

blocks.source: Now that we have completed this preliminary analysis of continuous one-one functions, it is possible to begin asking which important properties of a one-one function are inherited by its inverse. For continuity there is no problem.
blocks.translation: 对连续一一函数的初步分析已经完成，现在可以开始追问：一一函数的哪些重要性质会被它的反函数继承？对于连续性，毫无问题。

blocks.source: **THEOREM 3**
If $f$ is continuous and one-one on an interval, then $f^{-1}$ is also continuous.
blocks.translation: 如果 $f$ 在一个区间上连续且一一，那么 $f^{-1}$ 也连续。

blocks.source: **PROOF** We know by Theorem 2 that $f$ is either increasing or decreasing. We might as well assume that $f$ is increasing, since we can then take care of the other case by applying the usual trick of considering $-f$. We might as well assume our interval is open, since it is easy to see that a continuous increasing or decreasing function on any interval can be extended to one on a larger open interval.
blocks.translation: **证明** 由定理 2，我们知道 $f$ 不是递增就是递减。不妨假设 $f$ 递增，因为对另一种情形，可以用惯常的技巧，转而考虑 $-f$。也不妨假设这个区间是开区间，因为容易看出：任意区间上的连续递增或递减函数，都可以延拓成更大的开区间上的连续递增或递减函数。

blocks.source: We must show that

blocks.source: ## APPENDIX. PARAMETRIC REPRESENTATION OF CURVES
blocks.translation: ## 附录　曲线的参数表示

blocks.source: The material in this chapter serves to emphasize something that we noticed a long time ago—a perfectly nice looking curve need not be the graph of a function (Figure 1). In other words, we may not be able to describe it as the set of all points $(x,f(x))$. Of course, we might be able to describe the curve as the set of all points $(f(x),x)$; for example, the curve in Figure 1 is the set of all points $(x^2,x)$. But even this trick doesn’t work in most cases. It won’t allow us to describe the circle, consisting of all points $(x,y)$ with $x^2+y^2=1$, or an ellipse, and it can’t be used to describe a curve like the one in Figure 2.
blocks.translation: 本章的内容强调了我们很早就注意到的一点——一条看起来十分规整的曲线，不一定是某个函数的图像（图 1）。换句话说，我们也许无法将它描述为所有点 $(x,f(x))$ 组成的集合。当然，也许可以将曲线描述为所有点 $(f(x),x)$ 组成的集合；例如，图 1 中的曲线就是所有点 $(x^2,x)$ 的集合。但多数情况下，连这个技巧也行不通。它无法描述由所有满足 $x^2+y^2=1$ 的点 $(x,y)$ 组成的圆，也无法描述椭圆，更不能用来描述图 2 那样的曲线。

blocks.source: The simplest way of describing curves in the plane in general harks back to the physical conception of a curve as the path of a particle moving in the plane. At each time $t$, the particle is at a certain point, which has two coordinates; to indicate the dependence of these coordinates on the time $t$, we can call them $u(t)$ and $v(t)$. Thus, we end up with *two* functions. Conversely, given two functions $u$ and $v$, we can consider the curve consisting of all points $(u(t),v(t))$. This curve is said to be represented *parametrically* by $u$ and $v$, and the pair of functions $u$, $v$ is called a parametric representation of the curve. The curve represented parametrically by $u$ and $v$ thus consists of all pairs $(x,y)$ with $x=u(t)$ and $y=v(t)$. It is often described briefly as “the curve $x=u(t)$, $y=v(t)$.” Notice that the graph of a function $f$ can always be described parametrically, as the curve $x=t$, $y=f(t)$.
blocks.translation: 一般地描述平面曲线，最简单的办法是回到物理上的曲线概念：把它看作平面内运动质点的轨迹。每个时刻 $t$，质点都位于某一点，该点有两个坐标；为了表明这两个坐标依赖于时间 $t$，我们可以称它们为 $u(t)$ 和 $v(t)$。于是最终得到的是*两个*函数。反过来，给定两个函数 $u$ 和 $v$，就可以考虑由所有点 $(u(t),v(t))$ 组成的曲线。我们称这条曲线由 $u$ 和 $v$ 作*参数表示*，并称这一对函数 $u$、$v$ 为曲线的一个参数表示。因此，由 $u$ 和 $v$ 作参数表示的曲线，由所有满足 $x=u(t)$ 和 $y=v(t)$ 的数对 $(x,y)$ 组成。它常被简写为“曲线 $x=u(t)$，$y=v(t)$”。注意，函数 $f$ 的图像总能表示为参数曲线 $x=t$、$y=f(t)$。

blocks.source: Instead of considering a curve in the plane as defined by two functions, we can obtain a conceptually simpler picture if we broaden our original definition of function somewhat. Instead of considering a rule which associates a number with another number, we can consider a “function $c$ from real numbers to the plane,” i.e., a rule $c$ that associates, to each number $t$, a *point in the plane*, which we can denote by $c(t)$. With this notion, a curve is just a function from some interval of real numbers to the plane.
blocks.translation: 我们不必把平面曲线看成由两个函数定义的对象；只要稍微拓宽最初的函数定义，就能得到概念上更简单的图景。我们可以不再只考虑把一个数对应到另一个数的规则，而是考虑“从实数到平面的函数 $c$”，也就是一个规则 $c$，它把每个数 $t$ 对应到*平面上的一个点*，记作 $c(t)$。按照这种看法，曲线就是从某个实数区间到平面的函数。

blocks.translation: 还可以考虑函数

blocks.source: $$d(t)=c(p(t))=(c\circ p)(t),$$

where $p$ is now an ordinary function, from numbers to numbers. The new curve $d$ passes through the same points as $c$, except at different times; thus $p$ corresponds to a “reparameterization” of $c$. For
blocks.translation: 其中 $p$ 现在是一个从数到数的普通函数。新曲线 $d$ 经过的点与 $c$ 相同，只是经过的时刻不同；因此 $p$ 对应于 $c$ 的一次“重新参数化”。对于

blocks.source: $$\begin{aligned}c&=(u,v),\\d&=(u\circ p,v\circ p),\end{aligned}$$
we obtain
blocks.translation: 我们得到

blocks.source: $$\begin{aligned}d'(a)&=((u\circ p)'(a),(v\circ p)'(a))\\&=(p'(a)u'(p(a)),p'(a)v'(p(a)))\\&=p'(a)\cdot(u'(p(a)),v'(p(a)))\\&=p'(a)\cdot c'(p(a)),\end{aligned}$$
or simply
blocks.translation: 或者简写成

blocks.source: $$d'=p'\cdot(c'\circ p).$$

Notice that if $p(a)=a$, so that $d$ and $c$ actually pass through the same point at time $a$, then $d'(a)=p'(a)\cdot c'(a)$, so that the tangent vector $d'(a)$ is just a multiple of $c'(a)$. This means that the tangent line to $c$ at $c(a)$ is the same as the tangent line to the reparameterized curve $d$ at $d(a)=c(a)$. The one exception occurs
blocks.translation: 注意，如果 $p(a)=a$，那么 $d$ 和 $c$ 在时刻 $a$ 实际上经过同一个点，此时 $d'(a)=p'(a)\cdot c'(a)$，所以切向量 $d'(a)$ 只是 $c'(a)$ 的一个倍数。这意味着，$c$ 在 $c(a)$ 处的切线，与重新参数化后的曲线 $d$ 在 $d(a)=c(a)$ 处的切线相同。唯一的例外发生在

blocks.source: when $p'(a)=0$, since the tangent line for $d$ is then undefined, even though the tangent line for $c$ may be defined. For example, $d(t)=c(t^3)$ won’t have a tangent line defined at $t=0$, even though it’s merely a reparameterization of $c$.
blocks.translation: $p'(a)=0$ 时，因为这时 $d$ 的切线没有定义，尽管 $c$ 的切线可能有定义。例如，$d(t)=c(t^3)$ 在 $t=0$ 处不会有按上述方式定义的切线，尽管它不过是 $c$ 的一次重新参数化。

blocks.source: Finally, since we can define real-valued functions
blocks.translation: 最后，既然可以定义实值函数

blocks.source: $$\begin{aligned}(c\cdot d)(t)&=c(t)\cdot d(t),\\\det(c,d)(t)&=\det(c(t),d(t)),\end{aligned}$$
we ought to have formulas for the derivatives of these new functions. As you might guess, the proper formulas are
blocks.translation: 就应该有这些新函数的导数公式。正如你可能猜到的，正确的公式是

blocks.source: $$\begin{aligned}(c\cdot d)'(a)&=c(a)\cdot d'(a)+c'(a)\cdot d(a),\\{}[\det(c,d)]'(a)&=\det(c',d)(a)+\det(c,d')(a).\end{aligned}$$

These can be derived by straightforward calculations from the definitions in terms of the component functions. But it is more elegant to imitate the proof of the ordinary product rule, using the simple formulas in Problems 2 and 4 of Appendix 1 to Chapter 4, and, of course, the “standard trick” referred to above.
blocks.translation: 根据用分量函数表述的定义，直接计算就能推得这些公式。但更漂亮的办法是仿照普通乘积法则的证明，使用第 4 章附录 1 的习题 2 和 4 中的简单公式，当然也要用到上面提到的“惯常技巧”。

blocks.source: A *cycloid* is defined as the path traced out by a point on the rim of a rolling wheel of radius $a$. You can see a beautiful cycloid by pasting a reflector on the edge of a bicycle wheel and having a friend ride slowly in front of the headlights of your car at night. Lacking a car, bicycle, or trusting friend, you can settle instead for Figure 9.
blocks.translation: *摆线*定义为：一个半径为 $a$ 的轮子滚动时，轮缘上一点所描出的轨迹。把一个反光片贴在自行车轮缘上，夜间让一位朋友骑着车，缓缓经过你的汽车前灯前方，你就能看到一条美丽的摆线。如果缺少汽车、自行车，或者一位信任你的朋友，那就将就看看图 9 吧。

blocks.source: (a) Let $u(t)$ and $v(t)$ be the coordinates of the point on the rim after the wheel has rotated through an angle of $t$ (radians). This means that the arc of the wheel rim from $P$ to $Q$ in Figure 10 has length $at$. Since the wheel is rolling, $at$ is also the distance from $O$ to $Q$. Show that we have the parametric representation of the cycloid
blocks.translation: (a) 设轮子转过 $t$（弧度）角后，轮缘上该点的坐标为 $u(t)$ 和 $v(t)$。这意味着，图 10 中从 $P$ 到 $Q$ 的轮缘圆弧长度为 $at$。由于轮子在滚动，$at$ 也就是从 $O$ 到 $Q$ 的距离。证明，摆线具有如下参数表示：

blocks.source: $$\begin{aligned}u(t)&=a(t-\sin t)\\v(t)&=a(1-\cos t).\end{aligned}$$

Figure 11 shows the curves we obtain if the distance from the point to the center of the wheel is (a) less than the radius or (b) greater than the radius. In the latter case, the curve is not the graph of a function; at certain times the point is moving backwards, even though the wheel is moving forwards!
blocks.translation: 图 11 画出了点到轮心的距离 (a) 小于半径或 (b) 大于半径时得到的曲线。在后一种情形中，曲线不是函数的图像；尽管轮子一直向前运动，该点在某些时刻却在向后运动！
